05fec58b4c.viz_critic_note: The palette and title are well chosen, but overlapping rectangles hide or bury several states and the legend sits on Florida, so the map doesn't work as a choropleth.
05fec58b4c.encoding_auditor_note: The probe found no load or NaN errors and the geometry is sound (50 Polygons, correct winding fix), but the blue-sand-red ramp's lightness isn't monotonic and it only spans the observed 26–85 range of a stated 0–100 index, which misrepresents both order and magnitude. Missing values also aren't handled: color(undefined) is not given a no-data fill.
05fec58b4c.interaction_tester_note: The map had no errors or NaN and kept up with fast hovering. It scales down safely but becomes hard to read at phone width, and keyboard users can't reach any of the state data.

16256d39c5.viz_critic_note: A carefully styled dark-theme edge bundle with a restrained six-team palette and readable monospace labels, but the ring's uneven angular spacing and a garbled deprecated label make it feel less polished than its styling suggests.
16256d39c5.encoding_auditor_note: The edge bundle is honest and loads with no NaN geometry, and links are keyed, but dot area exaggerates size differences because the size scale doesn't start at zero, and team colours depend on row order.
16256d39c5.interaction_tester_note: The page is clean at load, on click and at phone width, but hover makes hundreds of DOM changes per pointer move, keyboard users can't reach the data, and the info panel covers the title on phones.

16c55eaf21.viz_critic_note: The palette and type are well chosen, but the state shapes overlap and hide each other, so this reads as a broken choropleth rather than a map.
16c55eaf21.encoding_auditor_note: The choropleth is honest: the domain comes from the data, joins are keyed, and the probe found no load or NaN problems, but the ramp's lightness reverses in the teal-to-yellow stretch and missing values would render as black, the darkest (highest-looking) color.
16c55eaf21.interaction_tester_note: Nothing broke when I loaded, hovered, clicked fast or resized, and the map reflows cleanly at phone width, but a keyboard can't reach any of the data.

19e129422b.viz_critic_note: The map is broken: the state polygons have wrong winding order, so they fill the whole frame with huge slivers, and the actual US map is a tiny dark knot in the middle.
19e129422b.encoding_auditor_note: A rewind bug swaps lat and lon in every polygon. As a result, 21 states disappear, 24 become full-frame rectangles, and 13 labels get NaN positions, so the choropleth shows no state in its real place.
19e129422b.interaction_tester_note: The choropleth is broken on first load: its polygons render inside-out so the whole plot is one flood of color, and 13 labels have NaN positions, so you can't read the map at any width.

1c861a4198.viz_critic_note: A working, well-thought-out linked parallel-coordinates and summary-table tool with a sensible muted region palette, but the layout runs out of room on the right, so the Elevation axis and the sparklines get squeezed and clipped.
1c861a4198.encoding_auditor_note: The encodings themselves are honest: every domain comes from the data, the log switch is guarded against zero and negatives, and the joins are keyed. But the keyed join for the sparse dots breaks on the update after it first runs, which can leave the linked views stale, and the blue brushed curve is scaled to its own peak, so it overstates the subset next to the grey full-data curve.
1c861a4198.interaction_tester_note: The page renders cleanly, but its main interaction, brushing, throws errors and leaves the count badge and the plot showing different selections. On top of that, hover causes an update storm, it overflows at phone width, and the keyboard can't reach the data.

1d3fdab6a3.viz_critic_note: A clean, well-built beeswarm with tidy filter pills and median markers, but the rows are too tall for the dots and the six hues repeat what the row labels already say.
1d3fdab6a3.encoding_auditor_note: The chart is honest with the current data: dots are equal-sized and x is linear, with no NaN geometry. It's brittle because the x domain and category list are hard-coded, so dots outside 30–220 or in an unknown category would be drawn off the axis or silently dropped.
1d3fdab6a3.interaction_tester_note: Nothing broke: no errors or NaN, no update storm, fast double clicks were safe, and the chart redraws cleanly at every width, but hovering over a circle does nothing and keyboard users can't reach the data.

32ff9ae98d.viz_critic_note: A clean, well-organized beeswarm with a clear title, colored toggle chips that double as the legend, and a sensible shared salary axis, though the swarms are too thin for their bands and points bunch against the left edge.
32ff9ae98d.encoding_auditor_note: The data is shown honestly: a beeswarm dot plot with a data-driven linear x domain (no baseline or area-scaling issue), keyed joins and no NaN geometry. The weak points are the hard-coded category list and no handling of empty or degenerate data.
32ff9ae98d.interaction_tester_note: The swarm plot survives fast pointer moves and double clicks with no errors, but at phone width it just shrinks until its labels can't be read, and keyboard users can reach the toggles but no data point.

3b98906e0f.viz_critic_note: A clean, well-built SPLOM with a coherent three-color palette and clear species separation, held back by repeated labels in every cell and a few crowded diagonal cells.
3b98906e0f.encoding_auditor_note: Honest and data-driven: bars start at a count of 0, domains come from the data, radius is constant, and the joins are keyed. The only real issue is unequal-width edge bins in the histograms, and nothing guards against edge cases such as empty data, where d3.extent returns undefined and the domains become NaN.
3b98906e0f.interaction_tester_note: No errors, NaN, update storm or double-click race, and brushing and keyboard focus both work, but at phone width the right column and legend are cut off with no way to scroll to them.

3f12f5c284.viz_critic_note: A correct, readable, fully specified SPLOM with clear species separation, but the palette is close to the default, the header is cramped, and the grid sits off-center in the frame.
3f12f5c284.encoding_auditor_note: The page loads with no NaN geometry. The encodings are honest: data-driven domains, 0-based stacked count histograms, keyed joins, fixed-size dots and categorical color. Two edge cases are unguarded: a null measurement plots at sx(0) and can land outside the panel, and if every value is equal the domain collapses and the histogram has no bin edges.
3f12f5c284.interaction_tester_note: The linked brushing held up under speed and double clicks with no errors or NaN, but at phone width half the matrix is clipped with no way to reach it, and nothing inside the chart is keyboard-reachable.

43ce4aefe1.viz_critic_note: A working, well-organized linked view with a useful sparkline table, but the parallel-coordinates panel is a dense, default-colored tangle whose tick labels get buried, so it reads as competent rather than designed.
43ce4aefe1.encoding_auditor_note: The parallel coordinates are honest and data-driven with keyed joins, and the transformed data loaded with no NaN geometry. The main flaw is the brushed-subset sparkline: blue bars scaled to their own peak sit on top of grey full-data bars on a different scale, which overstates how big the subset is.
43ce4aefe1.interaction_tester_note: No errors or NaN in hover, brush, click or resize at desktop width, but at phone width the main parallel-coordinates chart shrinks to a sliver and the table overflows, and nothing in the chart can be reached by keyboard.

46f6cf15ed.viz_critic_note: A deliberately styled radial edge bundle with a muted team palette and clear branch arcs, but the module labels crowd into the node dots, which makes it look unfinished.
46f6cf15ed.encoding_auditor_note: The layout and links come straight from the data and the geometry is clean (0 NaN), but the dot sizes use a scale that isn't anchored at zero, so they exaggerate size differences by about 1.8× even though the legend says area = size.
46f6cf15ed.interaction_tester_note: Nothing threw an error or produced NaN, but hover redraws on every pointer event and a fast mode toggle leaves leftover radial arcs in the tree view; also, the legend covers the chart at phone width and the data can't be reached by keyboard.

46feabdb5c.viz_critic_note: A tidy SPLOM with the correct 4×4 layout, clear diagonal labels and a prominent count badge, but its default-leaning palette and muddy overlapping histograms keep it short of deliberate design.
46feabdb5c.encoding_auditor_note: The scatterplot encodings are honest and data-driven, and the brushing is keyed by id, but the diagonal 'stacked' histograms actually overlap each other and the padded bin edges create partial-width edge bins, so the per-species histogram counts are hard to read correctly.
46feabdb5c.interaction_tester_note: The matrix holds up to fast pointer moves, double clicks and brushing with no errors, NaN or update storm, but keyboard users can't reach it at all and at phone width the labels and legend are clipped.

5630e5bc90.viz_critic_note: A capable linked parallel-coordinates and summary-table layout that is clearly structured, but the axis tick labels are buried under a dense six-hue line hairball, and the table has a lot of empty space.
5630e5bc90.encoding_auditor_note: Domains are data-driven and joins are keyed. But the subset histogram's y-scale is inflated against its ghost, one axis silently switches to log, and missing values break the line geometry.
5630e5bc90.interaction_tester_note: Load, hover, brushing and rapid double clicks all work with no errors or NaN, but at phone width the page overflows and the axes and table overlap into an unreadable mess, and keyboard users can't reach any of the data.

5802e3185f.viz_critic_note: A clean, well-made beeswarm with a warm off-white background and colored row labels that match the filter pills, but the swarms are squashed into thin strips, so most of the vertical space goes unused and the distribution shapes are hard to see.
5802e3185f.encoding_auditor_note: The chart is accurate for its current data: this beeswarm uses constant-radius dots and no length encoding, it uses a keyed join, and it passes the load and NaN checks. But the fixed [30, 220] domain and fixed category list mean it breaks under scaling, shifts, or new categories.
5802e3185f.interaction_tester_note: The chart held up under the speed tests: no errors or NaN, hover updated only about 0.3 times per pointer move with no long tasks, and it reflowed cleanly at every width. It loses points because keyboard users can't reach the data and the axis labels overlap at phone width.

6a5af9183d.viz_critic_note: A well-crafted sunburst with a harmonious four-hue palette and a clear outer headcount band, held back by truncated labels on arcs with room to spare, no labels on the team rings, and a legend that describes the encodings wrongly.
6a5af9183d.encoding_auditor_note: The budget angles in the sunburst are honest, but the outer headcount ring is scaled to each division's own maximum, and the paths are drawn with no key function, so small divisions look as big as large ones (lie factor about 2.75), the reading guide is wrong, and the layout depends on row order.
6a5af9183d.interaction_tester_note: Hover and rapid clicks are stable with no errors or NaN, but at phone width the chart shrinks to a roughly 45px thumbnail because the layout never stacks, and no arc can be reached with the keyboard.

6ba5053d71.viz_critic_note: A capable linked parallel-coordinates and summary-table layout. The table side looks clean, but the axes view is a dense tangle of six saturated colors that buries its own tick labels.
6ba5053d71.encoding_auditor_note: The scales are data-driven, the joins are keyed, and the probe found no NaN geometry. The main honesty problem is the subset sparkline bars: below 50% brushed they silently switch to a different y-scale from their ghost, so a subset bar can look taller than the full-data bar it belongs to.
6ba5053d71.interaction_tester_note: It holds up to fast moves, repeated brushing and double clicks, but at phone width the layout gets crushed into overlapping labels and numbers, and keyboard users can't reach any of the data.

7386e95c0d.viz_critic_note: The YlGnBu palette and the title are tidy, but the rectangular states overlap each other heavily, so the map looks broken and several states are hidden or unreadable.
7386e95c0d.encoding_auditor_note: The choropleth is honest. The probe found no NaN geometry, the ramp is data-driven with increasing lightness, and the joins are keyed; the weak points are the '0-100' subtitle, which doesn't match the 26-85 color domain, and no handling for missing or constant values.
7386e95c0d.interaction_tester_note: The page had no errors or NaN during load, hover, fast clicking or resizing. It loses points because nothing is reachable by keyboard and some state shapes cover others.

741808ae47.viz_critic_note: A clearly designed dual-encoding sunburst with a helpful explanatory side panel and a readable outer headcount ring, let down by clumsy label truncation and a bright, uneven team-ring palette.
741808ae47.encoding_auditor_note: The load and NaN probes pass and the budget sunburst is sound. The outer headcount ring misleads, though: it is normalized separately per division and its widths come from budget angles, so bar heights and areas can't be compared across the ring and the caption's claim doesn't hold.
741808ae47.interaction_tester_note: It loads cleanly with no NaN, and hover and rapid clicks cause no errors. But at phone width the fixed 768px chart doesn't adapt and about half of it plus the legend is cut off, and none of the data can be reached by keyboard.

758e2c697b.viz_critic_note: A capable linked parallel-coordinates and summary-table layout with a considered palette and a clear count badge, but the plot is overplotted, its interior tick labels are buried under the lines, and the table fills only the top third of its panel.
758e2c697b.encoding_auditor_note: The parallel coordinates are honest: domains come from the data, log is only used when lo > 0 and the unit label says '(log)', and joins are keyed. However, the sparkline overlays put subset bars on a separately normalized scale, so they misstate the subset's share of the whole, and missing values would be drawn as fake zeros.
758e2c697b.interaction_tester_note: Handles speed well (fast brushing, rapid clicks, no NaN), but at phone width the chart's axes pile on top of each other and the table is cut off, and keyboard users can't reach the chart at all.

7b90f7c531.viz_critic_note: A dark-theme sunburst with a controlled four-hue palette and a clear center total, but the heavy outer headcount ring dominates it, and the upside-down labels and missing team names make it hard to read without hovering.
7b90f7c531.encoding_auditor_note: Budget-as-angle is honest, but the headcount depth has a 16px floor and is normalized per division inside one shared ring, so depths can't be compared across divisions and the combined wedge area overstates big teams.
7b90f7c531.interaction_tester_note: It holds up under fast hovering and clicking with no errors or NaN, but keyboard users can't reach it, and at phone width the chart stays beside the text and gets too small to read.

9e1a5491aa.viz_critic_note: The palette and header are tidy, but the map's shapes overlap so badly that several states are hidden or mislabeled, which makes the choropleth unreadable as a map.
9e1a5491aa.encoding_auditor_note: Probe found no load errors and no NaN geometry. It's an honest choropleth: keyed join, data-driven extent, lightness-monotonic ramp, and correctly rewound CCW rings. The code doesn't handle missing values, and all-equal values collapse to one color.
9e1a5491aa.interaction_tester_note: The map loaded with no errors or NaN, survived fast hovering and double clicks, and scales at phone width, but it's unreadable at 375px with the legend cut off, and it can't be reached by keyboard at all.

a3728f0014.viz_critic_note: A clean, well-built SPLOM: the colorblind-safe palette and the stacked-histogram diagonal make the species separation easy to read, and a few axis and header details keep it from graphics-desk quality.
a3728f0014.encoding_auditor_note: The encodings are honest: domains come from the data, histograms start at 0, bins come from the data, the brush is linked by id, and the probe found no NaN at load or after the ×10, shuffle and drop tests. The weak spots are that missing values turn into 0, the species list is hard-coded, and the histograms have no count scale.
a3728f0014.interaction_tester_note: Load, brush, rapid clicks and resize all ran with no errors, no NaN and no update storm, but there's no keyboard access and the 375px layout clips labels and hides the selection controls.

aa5f1379eb.viz_critic_note: A clean, readable beeswarm with a clear title, a subtitle that explains how to use it, and neat filter pills, but it has lots of empty space and its color adds nothing the row labels don't already say.
aa5f1379eb.encoding_auditor_note: This is an honest beeswarm: the x domain comes from the data, dot radius is constant rather than tied to a value, the join is keyed, and the probe found no NaN geometry. Beeswarm drift is under 0.5k, and its only weak spots are the hard-coded category and color lists and the unguarded empty or degenerate data cases.
aa5f1379eb.interaction_tester_note: Nothing broke on load, hover, rapid clicking or any resize width, and the pointer sweep caused no storm; it loses points because you can't reach the data by keyboard and the x-axis labels crowd at phone width.

ae868ec58b.viz_critic_note: A carefully made radial edge bundle: team hues, visible branch hubs and dot styles for status turn the containment tree into something you can read, though the bundling in the middle is loose and a few details are rough.
ae868ec58b.encoding_auditor_note: The structure, links and keyed joins are honest, but dot size breaks the legend's 'area ~ size' claim: the square-root scale starts at the data minimum and a 3px floor, so differences look about 1.8× larger than they are.
ae868ec58b.interaction_tester_note: The page loads cleanly and has no NaN or click errors, but hover redraws on every pointer move and the chart shrinks to unreadable size at phone width, where the legend overlaps the caption.

b35bc8409b.viz_critic_note: A clean, readable beeswarm with good structure and an obvious entry point, but the six hue-per-row colors add nothing, and data at the $40k edge looks clamped or clipped.
b35bc8409b.encoding_auditor_note: This is an honest beeswarm (position-only encoding, data-driven extent domain, keyed join, no NaN on the real data), but it isn't robust to missing salaries (NaN circles) or categories outside the hard-coded list (silently dropped).
b35bc8409b.interaction_tester_note: Loading, hovering, fast pointer movement and rapid clicks produced no errors, no NaN and no update storm. It loses points because the chart only scales down on a phone instead of reflowing, and keyboard users can't reach the data points.

b37c965d2b.viz_critic_note: A readable, clearly structured sunburst in which the headcount outer ring makes budget-heavy vs people-heavy teams easy to see, though the leaf-ring colors are loud and the teams aren't labeled.
b37c965d2b.encoding_auditor_note: The budget rings are honest, but the headcount ring is scaled separately for each division and its segment areas grow with budget × headcount, so it misrepresents headcount across divisions.
b37c965d2b.interaction_tester_note: Hover and rapid clicks work with no errors or NaN, but the chart is a fixed 768px and gets cut off on a phone, and none of the data can be reached by keyboard.

b674da80f2.viz_critic_note: A clean, working parallel-coordinates dashboard with a tidy summary table, but the chart sits in only the middle of its panel, with a lot of empty space above and below, and the fully opaque lines bury the axis ticks.
b674da80f2.encoding_auditor_note: The main parallel-coordinates encoding is honest and fully data-driven with keyed joins, but the sparkline overlay puts each subset on its own normalised scale, which misstates its size against the full data, and `line.defined` checks the value after scaling, so missing values would show up as NaN or as fake zeros.
b674da80f2.interaction_tester_note: It survives fast use (brushing works, no NaN, no errors, no update storm, and rapid double clicks are handled), but it breaks at phone width: the layout doesn't reflow, the chart shrinks until it's unreadable, the table is cut off, and the axes can't be reached by keyboard.

b82024933d.viz_critic_note: A well-made sunburst: the muted four-hue palette with tints for each level and the separate headcount band make budget vs. people easy to compare at a glance, but the team level has no labels, so the chart's main point can only be read by hovering.
b82024933d.encoding_auditor_note: The budget sunburst is honest and fully driven by the data (the probe found no load errors and no NaN geometry), but the headcount band is scaled per division and its visible area mixes budget with headcount, so depths can't be fairly compared across divisions.
b82024933d.interaction_tester_note: The sunburst held up under fast hover, double clicks and resize with no errors or NaN, but keyboard users can't reach it and its labels are too small to read at phone width because the layout doesn't stack.

c5b915feb0.viz_critic_note: A clean, well-organized SPLOM that makes the species separation obvious at a glance, with a tidy header strip. The color and type are competent but only lightly customized.
c5b915feb0.encoding_auditor_note: The encodings are honest: domains come from the data, histograms start at zero, joins are keyed, and brushing is stored in data space. The weak spots are that missing values are silently plotted at 0 and the diagonal histograms have no count axis.
c5b915feb0.interaction_tester_note: There were no errors or NaN under hover, brushing, pointer storms, rapid clicks or resizing, and the brush left a selection. The score is held back because nothing in the plot can be reached by keyboard and the layout is cramped and clipped at phone width.

d5aa068b56.viz_critic_note: A clean, legible beeswarm with useful median markers and tidy filter chips, let down by dots clipped at the left edge and tall bands that are mostly empty.
d5aa068b56.encoding_auditor_note: The beeswarm is honest: salary maps to position on a data-driven domain, the circles are a fixed size, the join is keyed, and medians are computed from the data. The hard-coded category list and headcount make it crash or mislead when a category is missing.
d5aa068b56.interaction_tester_note: The page stays clean under fast hover, rapid double clicks and resizing, with no errors or NaN, but it has hidden horizontal overflow at narrow widths and keyboard users can't reach the data.

d93b8415f3.viz_critic_note: The YlGnBu palette is chosen well and the page reads cleanly, but the map is a heap of overlapping, tilted rectangles, and with no labels you can't tell one state from another.
d93b8415f3.encoding_auditor_note: The load and NaN checks were clean. The choropleth is honest overall: it uses a lightness-monotonic YlGnBu ramp, a keyed join, and a legend that matches the data. Its weak points are that the color domain is stretched to the data extent even though the page claims a 0-100 scale, and that missing values would render black instead of as 'no data'.
d93b8415f3.interaction_tester_note: Load, fast hover, rapid clicks and resizing to phone width all ran with no errors or NaN; it loses points because keyboard users can't reach any of the data.

e18a20a304.viz_critic_note: A clean SPLOM that works and does what was asked, with histograms on the diagonal and clear species separation, but it uses default-looking colors and repeats the same axis labels in every cell.
e18a20a304.encoding_auditor_note: The encodings are honest, with data-driven domains, a zero-based histogram count axis, keyed dot joins and no NaN geometry, but the legend's species lookup assumes each id equals its array position, which breaks when rows are shuffled or missing.
e18a20a304.interaction_tester_note: The scatterplot matrix handles fast brushing and double clicks without errors, but a keyboard can't reach the data, there's no hover feedback, and at phone width the charts shrink to near-unreadable size with the legend cut off.

e360068fdc.viz_critic_note: A well-made dark-theme radial edge bundle: six restrained team hues, clearly readable leaf labels, and a legend that explains its encodings. The bundling itself is its weakest part, because the internal branch nodes are drawn as dots and the curves pinch into those points.
e360068fdc.encoding_auditor_note: The graph structure is drawn honestly and geometry is clean, but dot size is an additive-offset sqrt with no domain or legend key, which understates size differences by about 45%, and radial order depends on file order.
e360068fdc.interaction_tester_note: Solid under speed and rapid clicks, with no errors or NaN, but it only scales down at phone width, where the title overlaps the layout toggle and labels are unreadable, and most modules can't be reached by keyboard.

f2b81aeed2.viz_critic_note: A clean, well-organized dark radial bundle with a restrained six-team palette and clear team grouping, but the bundles themselves are so faint that the dependency structure, which is the point of the chart, is hard to see before you hover.
f2b81aeed2.encoding_auditor_note: The topology, keyed joins, color legend and link encoding all hold up, but the node-size encoding uses a sqrt scale with a non-zero domain and range: it exaggerates area differences by about 1.4× and breaks with negative radii at sizes near 0.
f2b81aeed2.interaction_tester_note: It holds up under fast hover, double clicks and resizing with no errors or NaN, but there's no keyboard access to the data and at phone width the chart shrinks until labels can't be read and the view toggle covers the title.

f8525f8c1d.viz_critic_note: This is a solid, readable radial bundle with a restrained six-team palette and clear branch nodes. The header is crowded, the bundling is loose, and the spacing between sectors is uneven, so it falls short of looking designed.
f8525f8c1d.encoding_auditor_note: The chart is honest: radius uses a sqrt scale with a zero-based, data-driven domain, the categorical colours are keyed by team, and the probe found no NaN geometry. The weak spots are a 3px size floor that could distort skewed data, no size legend, and a layout that assumes names are exactly three levels deep.
f8525f8c1d.interaction_tester_note: Loads cleanly with no NaN and survived rapid clicks, but hover redraws the whole bundle on every pointer move, the chart doesn't reflow at phone width (labels unreadable, toggle clipped), and modules can't be reached by keyboard.

fc16be3a86.viz_critic_note: A polished dark-theme sunburst with a coordinated four-hue palette and a clear center total. The outer headcount band is readable against its dark track, but the chart has no title, the team level has no labels, and the rotated labels make it harder to read.
fc16be3a86.encoding_auditor_note: The budget angles are honest, but the headcount ring uses a separate scale per division plus a 6px false baseline, so equal-looking bars can be headcounts almost 3× apart. The probe found no load errors and no NaN geometry.
fc16be3a86.interaction_tester_note: The radial chart is solid: no errors or NaN, rapid double clicks are safe, and it scales cleanly to phone width, but you can't reach it with the keyboard.
